newsitem.title: USA: Toxic lake algae near New Orleans seen as threat.
newsitem.headline: Toxic lake algae near New Orleans seen as threat.

text.p: A blue-green algae that produces hazardous toxins is spreading across Lake Pontchartrain near New Orleans and is a threat to animals and people, state health officials said Tuesday.
Dr. Jimmy Guidry, the state health officer, warned people to avoid using areas of the lake affected by the surface algae and to keep animals away.

The algae bloom has been spreading across the lake since May. It is a product of 3 trillion gallons of polluted Mississippi River floodwaters released into the normally brackish lake this spring to take pressure off the mainline levees in New Orleans, environmentalists said.
Up to two-thirds of the vast lake has been affected, but the size of the algae bloom fluctuates as wind, water currents and other weather conditions change, Guidry said.

The algae, identified by scientists as Anabena and Microcystis, produce a hepatotoxin capable of causing severe vomiting, diarrhea and liver damage. People allergic to the hepatotoxin could suffer respiratory problems and rashes if they touch or inhale even small amounts of algae, Guidry said.
He said dogs, cats and other animals have died after drinking such water in other parts of the United States and the world.
The algae is also causing fish kills in some areas, authorities said. Further tests are being conducted to determine if toxins affecting the nervous system are being released.
